metaDescription: Learn how to configure and save a reusable order preset in TradingView, including market units, risk settings, and profit and loss projections.
intro: Order presets in TradingView let you save a reusable trading template so you don't have to manually re-enter the same settings for similar trades. This guide covers configuring market units, risk settings, and saving the preset for future use.

steps.heading: Open the trading panel
steps.body: Click the trade button on your chart to open the trading panel where order presets are configured.

steps.heading: Adjust market units
steps.body: Specify the number of units for your order, tailored to your investment goals and market analysis.

steps.heading: Set your risk parameters
steps.body: Configure the financial exposure you're willing to accept, aligning it with your risk tolerance and strategy.

steps.heading: Review profit and loss projections
steps.body: Check the calculated projections to make sure they align with your financial objectives before saving.

steps.heading: Save the order preset
steps.body: Once your settings are configured, save them as a reusable preset instead of re-entering the same parameters each time.

steps.heading: Name and reuse your preset
steps.body: Give the preset a name that reflects its purpose or strategy, and apply it quickly to future trades.

faq.question: What is an order preset on TradingView?
faq.answer: It's a saved template of your trade settings, including units and risk parameters, that you can reuse instead of manually re-entering details each time.

faq.question: Can I edit a saved order preset later?
faq.answer: Yes, you can edit your presets anytime your trading strategy evolves.

faq.question: Where do I configure the risk settings?
faq.answer: Risk settings are adjusted within the trading panel when you're setting up your order details.

faq.question: Does the preset include profit and loss calculations?
faq.answer: Yes, you can review profit and loss projections as part of configuring your preset before saving it.

faq.question: Can I create multiple presets for different strategies?
faq.answer: Yes, you can save multiple presets with different names to match different trading strategies.
